paper_metadata.title: Design and coherent strengthening of ultra-high strength refractory high entropy alloys based on laser additive manufacturing

evidence.quote: The WNbMoTa-based refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) is expected to become a new generation of high-temperature materials

TN20 [...] RHEAs were formed by self-developed LPBF equipment. The wavelength of the laser is 1064 nm and the spot is 25 um. The substrate is titanium alloy substrate, the preheating temperature is 200 C, and argon of 99.99% purity is injected into the equipment cavity as a protective gas. The forming process of the alloys is as follows: power 350 W, layer thickness 50 um, scanning speed 350 mm/s, scan spacing 40 um; between layers, the laser scanning direction is rotated 67
Due to the high content of low melting point elements, the scanning speed of TN25 alloy was changed to 300 mm/s, and other process parameters remain unchanged.

attributes.composition: rich in W, Nb, Mo; 8.5 at.% Ti, small amount of Ta and Ni dissolved

evidence.quote: the XRD peaks of TN20 alloy show not only BCC structure matrix phase but also B2 structure grain boundary phase.
region 1 of the network distribution is the matrix phase of the BCC structure, which is rich in W, Nb and Mo elements, while 8.5% Ti and a small amount of Ta and Ni are solidly dissolved.

attributes.composition: rich in Ti and Ni, 10 at.% Nb dissolved

evidence.quote: TN20 alloy is composed of BCC matrix phase and grain boundary phase containing three different structures, which are B2 TiNi phase, Ni55Nb25Ti15Ta5 phase generating stacking faults and Ni70Ti20Nb10 secondary precipitated phase.
The 2 region embedded in the matrix phase is the TiNi phase with B2 structure, which is rich in Ti and Ni elements, and 10% Nb element is solidly dissolved.
The long strip region 3 occurred stacking faults after TN20 alloy LPBF forming, and its composition is Ni55Nb25Ti15Ta5.

attributes.morphology: secondary precipitated phase with nanoscale punctate coherent precipitates

evidence.quote: Region 4 is the secondary precipitated phase in B2 phase, with Ni70Ti20Nb10 as its component.
It can be seen that the matrix phase structure of TN20 alloy is dendritic. The growth of dendrites has no obvious direction, and the secondary arms of different dendrites interlock with each other.

attributes.morphology: fine crystal region in center of molten pool

evidence.quote: The grain distribution of the four alloys showed fine crystal region in the center of the molten pool, and coarse crystal region in the overlapping region of two molten pools. The grain sizes of TN10, TN15, TN20, and TN25 alloys are 6.22 +/- 3.45 um, 6.25 +/- 3.82 um, 5.84 +/- 2.95 um, and 6.53 +/- 3.93 um respectively.

attributes.morphology: coarse grains in overlapping region of two molten pools
attributes.location: overlapping region of two molten pools

evidence.quote: the grain distribution of the four alloys showed fine crystal region in the center of the molten pool, and coarse crystal region in the overlapping region of two molten pools.
The high-resolution and electron diffraction images of Fig. 7 (d) and (e) both show that the Ni55Nb25Ti15Ta5 phase has typical stacking fault characteristics.
There are not too many unmelted particles (white granular) in TN10, TN15 and TN20 alloys, while there are more unmelted W and Mo particles in TN25 alloys.
The TN10 and TN25 alloys have a small number of pore defects (black holes), while the TN15 and TN20 alloys are relatively dense.
The TN10 and TN25 alloys have a small number of pore defects (black holes), while the TN15 and TN20 alloys are relatively dense.
The optimal design of yield strength of matrix phase is realized by means of solid solution strengthening principle.
The microstructure bonding interface of TN20 alloy is strengthened by the coherent matching between B2 grain boundary phase and matrix phase.
the secondary phase and its nanocrystalline precipitated phase in grain boundary B2 phase can strengthen the grain boundary phase by the pinning effect.

mechanisms.name: crack suppression / healing by grain boundary phase

evidence.quote: After the matrix phase cracks due to high thermal stress, the flow TiNi-rich grain boundary phases precipitate to fill the cracks.
